drivers.name: Barco Pulse Projector
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Barco Pulse-platform laser projectors (F70 / F80 / F90, UDX, UDM, HDX 4K, I600, G62 / G100, XDL and other Pulse models) over the Pulse JSON-RPC API on TCP 9090. Live push updates for power, source, shutter, laser power and picture settings; source picker built from the projector's own input list; lens shift / zoom / focus; test patterns; environment temperatures; and a raw property/method escape hatch for the full Pulse API.

help.overview: Barco Pulse projectors speak JSON-RPC 2.0 on TCP 9090. The driver subscribes to the projector's change notifications, so power, source, shutter, laser power and picture values update live. The source picker offers the projector's own input list (read at connect). Lens shift / zoom / focus move by motor steps; models without a motorized lens answer those commands with an error, which is reported but harmless. The Get Property / Set Property / Invoke Method commands expose the full Pulse API for anything not surfaced as a named command.
help.setup:
1. Connect the projector's LAN port and give it a fixed IP (OSD: System Settings > Communication > LAN).
2. In OpenAVC, enter the IP. Leave port at 9090.
3. Leave the API pass code empty — it is only needed when the projector's API access has been restricted with a code.
4. ECO standby powers the network interface down, so a projector in ECO cannot be reached over the API. For fully controllable rooms leave ECO disabled (the Eco Standby device setting), or pair a Wake-on-LAN device to wake it.

compatible_models.notes: These families' Pulse API catalogs were used to build the driver (F80 End User v1.7, UDX Power User v1.7, F90 protocol manual 601-0421). The command surface is the shared Pulse API; per-model availability of lens motors, ECO mode and alarm state varies and the driver tolerates absent features.

Barco lists these as Pulse-platform projectors (same JSON-RPC API, per-family catalog editions). Expected to work identically; not verified against hardware. The Pulse API self-describes — use the Get Property / Invoke Method commands with the projector's own catalog for model-specific extras.

drivers.name: BenQ Projector
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls BenQ projectors using BenQ's RS232 Command Control protocol over the network (TCP 8000) or direct RS-232. Covers the install and large-venue families (LK / LU / LH / PU / PW / PX / L series) and the wider BenQ line that shares the same command table. Power, source select, volume and mute, picture mode, picture adjustment steps, color temperature, aspect ratio, blank, freeze, OSD menu navigation, light source mode and custom light level, lens memories, and installer settings (direct power on, quick auto search, high altitude, standby network). Polls for status.

help.overview: BenQ projectors speaking the BenQ RS232 Command Control protocol — the install / large-venue LK, LU, LH, PU, PW, PX, and L series and most other BenQ models with a LAN or RS-232 control port. Power, source, audio, picture controls, blank/freeze, OSD navigation, light source (lamp/laser) modes, lens memories, and installer settings. Polls every 30 seconds. For commands not exposed here, use Send Raw Command with the command table from your model's "RS232 Command Control Installation Guide" on BenQ's support site.
help.setup:
1. Network control: connect the projector's LAN port, note its IP
   address from the Network menu, and add it here with TCP port
   8000.
2. To keep network control available while the projector is off,
   turn on Standby Settings > Network on the projector (or write
   the Standby Network device setting once connected).
3. Serial control: connect the RS-232 port (or a serial bridge) at
   the baud rate shown in the projector's OSD (9600 default on most
   models), 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit.
4. Volume and custom light level ranges vary by model — check your
   model's guide or the OSD for the valid span.
help.connection: If the projector is powered off, its LAN control port only answers when Standby Settings > Network is On in the projector's menu.

compatible_models.notes: Each of these models has a published BenQ RS232 Command Control guide with the same command grammar. The guides carry a per-model Support column — a command a given model doesn't implement answers "*Unsupported item#", which the driver ignores. Most other BenQ network/serial-controllable projectors (including the home-cinema W series) share the same protocol and are expected to work.

drivers.name: Christie Projector
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Christie commercial projectors using the Christie Serial API on TCP 3002. Supports the M, J, HS, H, GS, G, and E series families and their derivatives. Power, shutter, fade-to-black, input select, test patterns, brightness/contrast, freeze, orientation, lamp mode, lamp intensity, and lens focus. Polls for status; the projector also reports model, firmware, and projector hours.

help.overview: Christie commercial projectors that speak the Christie Serial API (M Series, J Series, HS / H Series, GS / G Series, E Series, Roadie). Power, shutter, fade-to-black, input select, brightness, contrast, freeze, orientation, test patterns, lamp mode, lamp intensity, and lens focus. Polls every 30 seconds for status. For commands not exposed here, use Send Raw Command — the full command list is in the Christie Serial API Technical Reference for your projector series.
help.setup:
1. Connect the projector to your network. 2. On the projector menu, enable Ethernet and note the IP address. 3. The Christie Serial API listens on TCP 3002 by default and does
   not require authentication.
4. Set the projector's "Serial Mode" / "Serial API" to enabled if
   it is not already on. (M Series MENU > Configuration >
   Communications > Network Settings.)
5. The Input Select command takes a two-digit slot+input code
   (e.g. 12 = slot 1 input 2). The slot/input map is on the back
   panel of the projector.

compatible_models.notes: All series share the same (CODE) message format and the core power / shutter / input / image controls. Series-specific features (e.g. laser-light controls on HS, lens-shift codes on GS) are not exposed here; use send_command with the series' published command list when needed. Boxer / Inspire / 4KHS / Crimson use a newer JSON / Christie API and require a different driver — they are not covered here.

drivers.name: Epson Projector (ESC/VP21)
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Epson business and installation projectors over ESC/VP21 wrapped in ESC/VP.net on TCP port 3629. Power, input, A/V mute, freeze, aspect ratio, color mode, lamp hours, and remote-key passthrough.

help.overview: ESC/VP21 is Epson's text-based projector control protocol. Over the network it runs inside ESC/VP.net on TCP port 3629 — the driver handles the binary handshake transparently. Most modern Epson projectors respond to PJLink as well, but the native ESC/VP21 surface gives access to color mode, aspect ratio, freeze, image-quality numerics, and the full virtual remote keypad — none of which PJLink covers.
help.setup:
1. Connect the projector to the network and assign a static IP.
2. In the projector's network menu, enable 'Network Standby' (or 'Standby Mode = Communication On' on older units) so the projector responds to network commands while powered off.
3. Confirm 'Control Communications' (some menus call this 'PJLink' or 'ESC/VP.net') is enabled.
4. Optional: if the projector has an ESC/VP.net password set in the web setup, this driver does not currently send a password — disable it for control use, or use the device's web UI for one-off setup.

models: EB-L Series (EB-L200X, EB-L520W, EB-L630U, EB-L1075U, EB-L1100U)
compatible_models.notes: ESC/VP21 is shared across Epson's business and installation projector lines. Per-model variation is in which input codes the projector actually accepts (e.g. older units have no HDBaseT input). The driver lets the user pick from the union of all common codes; unsupported codes return ERR on the projector, which the driver logs at debug.

drivers.name: PJLink Class 1 Projector
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls any PJLink Class 1 compatible projector.

help.overview: Universal projector control via the PJLink Class 1 standard. Works with 100+ models from Epson, NEC, Panasonic, Sony, Christie, Hitachi, BenQ, Optoma, Canon, Barco, Fujifilm, and Vivitek. Where a brand has its own dedicated driver in the catalog (Panasonic PT, Sharp NEC, Sony VPL, Epson ES/VP, Barco Pulse), prefer that driver — it generally exposes more capability than PJLink's universal subset.
help.setup:
1. Enable network control on the projector (varies by manufacturer)
2. Assign a static IP address to the projector
3. If authentication is enabled, set the PJLink password
4. Default port is 4352 (PJLink standard)

compatible_models.notes: PJLink is a JBMIA cross-vendor standard. Any projector advertising PJLink Class 1 (or Class 2) support in its datasheet should work with this driver. Brand-specific drivers (when available) generally expose more — lamp diagnostics, vendor-specific picture modes, faster polling, extended status — and should be preferred over PJLink.

Panasonic commercial PT- series. Datasheets confirm Class 1 + 2. The dedicated `panasonic_pt` driver covers more (NTCONTROL Protocol 2 with md5 session auth, lamp/laser diagnostics) — prefer it when available for the same model.

models: Sharp XP Series (XP-P701U, XP-P621U, XP-X171Q, XP-V series)
compatible_models.notes: Combined Sharp NEC Display Solutions lineup (post-2020 merger). Sharp XP series and NEC PA/PX/PH/ME/M/NP series. JBMIA-registered for Sharp XP models. NaViSet Administrator is the vendor's own richer control software; PJLink is the open cross-vendor fallback. The dedicated `sharp_nec_projector` driver covers more (NEC native command set, lens/zoom/shift control).

Sony VPL data projectors. Configure via Web Advanced Menu → PJLINK. Up to 3 controllers can connect simultaneously. The dedicated `sony_vpl` driver (ADCP / SDAP) covers more (SHA-256 challenge-response auth, native lens controls).
JBMIA-registered as Class 2. Modern Epson commercial laser/lamp models. The dedicated `epson_escvp` driver covers more (ESC/VP command set, faster, brand-specific picture modes).
BenQ commercial install projectors with the network function enabled. Activated via the Network setting on the projector menu.

models: Professional J-Series (JEV, JSV, JNV, JWV, JTV, JCV, JPV)
compatible_models.notes: JBMIA-registered as Class 2. Optoma commercial / professional install projectors.
Christie commercial laser and lamp projectors. PJLink alongside Christie's native serial / IP API. Some models require enabling network IP control before PJLink will respond.
Barco F-series and Loop projectors. PJLink is a fallback to Barco's native Pulse REST API which exposes more capability.
Hitachi commercial projectors with the network/LAN module fitted. Not all Hitachi models include networking — check the datasheet.
Canon XEED commercial install projectors. Canon's product literature lists PJLink as a supported network control method.
JBMIA-registered as Class 2. Fujifilm folded-light-path ultra-short-throw commercial projectors.
Vivitek (Delta Electronics) commercial install projectors with the network function. Confirm PJLink in the model's datasheet.

drivers.name: Optoma Projector
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Optoma projectors over Optoma's RS232/LAN command protocol (Telnet port 23 or direct RS-232). Power, input select, A/V mute, shutter, audio, display modes, aspect, brightness/contrast, keystone, motorized lens with lens memories, remote-key navigation, light-source hours, and live fault notifications. Covers the ZU/ZK installation and large-venue laser series and other Optoma models sharing the published command table — the full brand feature set beyond what generic PJLink offers.

help.overview: Optoma's own control protocol — the same ~XX command set over the LAN (Telnet) or RS-232. Compared to PJLink it adds display modes, shutter, motorized lens control with position memories, keystone, remote-key navigation, light-source hours, and live fault reporting (fan, thermal, light source). The projector pushes power and fault transitions as they happen; other state is polled.
help.setup:
1. Connect the projector's LAN port and give it a static IP (or a DHCP reservation).
2. In the projector's Network / Communications menu make sure Telnet control is enabled (on most models it is on by default alongside the web control page).
3. Set Standby Power Mode to 'Communication' (some menus say 'Active' or 'Network Standby') so the projector still answers — and can be powered on — while in standby. The eco '0.5W' standby powers the network module down completely.
4. Serial control instead: connect the RS-232 port (9600 8N1 on most models; newer large-venue units default to 19200 — match the projector's Serial Port Baud Rate setting).
5. Leave Projector ID at 0 unless you have assigned IDs on an RS-232 chain; ID 0 addresses any projector.
help.connection: A projector in eco (0.5W) standby does not answer on the network at all — set Standby Power Mode to Communication so power_on works remotely. Power on/off feedback can take 6-10 seconds; the driver waits accordingly.

models: EH / WU / X / W business series
compatible_models.notes: Optoma publishes the same command grammar across its range; each model's RS232 Protocol Function List documents its supported subset, and a command a model lacks answers F (ignored by the driver). Lens shift/zoom/focus and lens memories need a motorized lens (ZK/ZU install and large-venue models); the shutter commands need a mechanical shutter. Volume range is 0-10 on most models, 0-15 on some.

drivers.name: Panasonic PT-MZ / PT-RZ Projector
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Panasonic PT-MZ (LCD) and PT-RZ (DLP) professional installation projectors via the NTCONTROL TCP protocol (Protocol 2). Power, input, shutter / AV mute, freeze, and operating-hours readout. Supports Panasonic's MD5 session-challenge authentication so the projector keeps its default Web Control admin password.

help.overview: Panasonic NTCONTROL (Protocol 2) is the TCP control channel shared across all Panasonic professional projectors. It runs on TCP 1024 by default with optional MD5 challenge-response authentication tied to the projector's Web Control admin account.
help.setup:
1. Connect the projector to the network and assign a static IP.
2. In the projector's main menu, set [Network] -> [Network Control] -> [Command Control] = ON. The default command port is 1024.
3. Open the projector's Web Control page in a browser. Set or change the Administrator-Authorized password (default username is ``admin1``, default password is ``panasonic``).
4. In OpenAVC, enter the projector's IP and the Web Control admin username and password. If you left the password blank in the projector's web UI (non-protected mode), leave the password field empty here too.

compatible_models.notes: Protocol 2 / NTCONTROL is the same on every Panasonic professional projector — the universal command surface (power, input select, shutter, freeze, operating hours) is consistent. Per-model variation is which physical inputs are present; the driver exposes the union and the projector returns ``ERR2`` for inputs it doesn't have, which the driver logs at debug.

drivers.name: Sanyo / EIKI / Boxlight Projector (RS-232 Serial)
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Sanyo-built projectors that use Sanyo's "Basic Serial Command" RS-232 protocol: Sanyo PLC, EIKI EK / LC, and Boxlight (Eco / Boston / ProjectoWrite) lines. Works on a direct serial port or through a serial bridge. Power, input select, blank, freeze, image modes, audio, zoom, keystone, on-screen navigation, and power management, with polled power / input / lamp-hours / temperature / model status. Baud and cable type vary by model (commonly 19200; both configurable).

help.overview: EIKI EK-series projector over RS-232 (the compact "C-command" protocol: "C" + a 2-character code + carriage return). Works on a direct serial port or through a serial bridge (choose "Through a bridge" in Connection settings and pick the bridge's RS-232 port). Power, inputs, blank, freeze, image modes, audio, zoom, keystone, navigation, power management, and polled status.
help.setup:
1. Connect the projector's RS-232 port (or wire it to a serial bridge)
   with an RS-232 CROSS (null-modem) cable.
2. Serial settings are 19200 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit,
   no flow control.
3. Through a bridge, the binding's 19200 8N1 is applied to the line
   automatically.
help.connection: The protocol requires a crossover (null-modem) cable between the controller/bridge and the projector. Status reads return on/standby, current input, lamp hours, internal temperatures, and the model name.

compatible_models.notes: Hardware-validated: two-way RS-232 control confirmed against an EK-307W (CR5 model read returns "Coral-EK-307W") at 19200 8N1 over a Global Cache iTach IP2SL serial bridge with a crossover cable.
EIKI EK / LC series projectors using the Sanyo Basic Serial Command protocol (same C00 / CRx command set). Verify baud and cable type per model before relying on it.
Sanyo PLC series, the origin of this "Basic Serial Command" protocol. Core power / input / status commands are shared; a few EK-era inputs here do not apply. Verify baud and cable type per model.
Boxlight (Sanyo-built) lines using the same C-command protocol. Note some Boxlight models (e.g. Eco Series) want a DIRECT cable rather than a crossover. Verify per model.

drivers.name: Sharp NEC Projector
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Sharp NEC projectors via the NEC binary control protocol over TCP. Compatible with P, PA, PE, PV, PX, ME, and M series projectors.

help.overview: Full-featured Sharp NEC projector control using the proprietary binary protocol on TCP port 7142. Power, input selection, picture/sound/OSD mute, freeze, shutter, volume, brightness, contrast, sharpness, aspect ratio, eco mode, lens control (zoom/focus/shift), lens memory presets, lamp/laser hours, filter hours, and detailed error status.
help.setup:
1. Connect the projector to the network
2. Enable LAN control in the projector's network settings
3. Assign a static IP address to the projector
4. Default control port is 7142
5. This driver can coexist with PJLink (port 4352)
6. Set Standby Mode to 'Network Standby' or 'Sleep' to allow power-on via network
7. Input terminal codes vary by model — unsupported inputs are rejected gracefully

compatible_models.notes: Verified on hardware.
Per NEC protocol manual. Specific models like NP-P506QL fall under P series.

drivers.name: Sony VPL Projector (ADCP)
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Sony VPL professional installation projectors over Sony's Advanced Display Control Protocol (ADCP) on TCP port 53595. Power, input, blank, freeze, picture mode, aspect ratio, image-quality (contrast / brightness / colour / sharpness), and the universal remote-key set. Supports SHA-256 challenge-response authentication so the projector can keep its default auth-on web setting.

help.overview: ADCP is Sony's text-based control protocol for professional VPL projectors. It runs on TCP 53595 with optional SHA-256 challenge-response authentication. The driver covers the universal command surface (power, input, blank, freeze, picture mode, image quality, aspect, remote keys) and surfaces the projector's reported power and error state.
help.setup:
1. Connect the projector to the network via its LAN or HDBaseT terminal and assign it a static IP.
2. In the projector's main menu, set Standby Mode = Standard so the projector responds to network commands while powered down.
3. Open the projector's web setup page. The default ADCP password is ``Projector`` — change it to something private.
4. In OpenAVC, enter the projector's IP and the ADCP password. Leave port at 53595.

compatible_models.notes: ADCP is the same on every VPL professional / installation projector — the command surface is consistent, the variation is which inputs and picture modes a given chassis exposes. The driver lets the user pick from the union of all inputs / modes; unsupported values return err_val on the projector, which the driver logs but does not raise.
